articles.title: Inscrições para o Bolsa-Atleta 2026 em Macaé terminam nesta sexta-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Atletas e paratletas têm até amanhã para garantir cadastro online e concorrer ao auxílio financeiro mensal de até R$ 1.500.
articles.summary: Atletas e paratletas têm até amanhã para garantir cadastro online e concorrer ao auxílio financeiro mensal de até R$ 1.500.
articles.body:
Prazo para concorrer ao benefício municipal termina nesta sexta-feira (9) — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Terminam nesta sexta-feira (9) as inscrições para o processo seletivo do programa Bolsa-Atleta 2026 em Macaé. Os interessados devem efetuar o cadastro exclusivamente de forma online, por meio do Sistema Eletrônico de Informações (SEI) da prefeitura. O benefício, coordenado pela Secretaria Municipal de Esportes, é voltado a atletas e paratletas residentes no município, com idade mínima de 10 anos, que estejam em plena atividade e disputem competições estaduais, nacionais, internacionais ou mundiais vinculadas a federações e confederações oficiais.

O programa contempla modalidades olímpicas, paralímpicas e de rendimento, oferecendo um auxílio financeiro mensal divididos em quatro faixas de enquadramento. A categoria Individual/Coletiva A garante R$ 500 mensais para participantes de provas federadas e confederadas. A categoria B concede R$ 750 por mês para quem alcançou até o terceiro lugar em competições estaduais. Atletas com destaque em torneios nacionais ou internacionais recebem R$ 1.000 mensais na categoria C, enquanto a categoria D destina R$ 1.500 mensais para quem conquistou pódio (até a 3ª colocação) em competições mundiais. Cada competidor poderá receber apenas uma bolsa em 2026, prevalecendo a de maior valor em caso de múltiplos enquadramentos.

Inscrições devem ser finalizadas no sistema eletrônico da prefeitura com envio de documentos — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Para realizar a inscrição antes do encerramento do prazo, o candidato precisa ter o Cadastro de Acesso Externo ao SEI validado antes de anexar os arquivos. A documentação exigida inclui cópia do RG e CPF, comprovante de residência atualizado, foto 3x4, atestado médico original emitido há no máximo seis meses, comprovante de matrícula e frequência para atletas em idade escolar, e declaração da entidade desportiva comprovando o vínculo do esportista. Além disso, é obrigatório apresentar o Plano Esportivo Anual com metas e calendário de provas, além de declarações de não recebimento de salário do clube ou patrocínio público e privado. Para menores de 18 anos, todos os formulários devem ser assinados pelos responsáveis legais.

As provas utilizadas como comprovação devem constar no calendário oficial das federações ou confederações da modalidade. Após a conclusão e o envio dos arquivos legíveis no portal, o sistema SEI gera automaticamente um número de processo eletrônico, que serve como comprovante definitivo de inscrição e deve ser guardado para acompanhamento. A ausência de qualquer item obrigatório acarretará desclassificação documental. O Edital Bolsa-Atleta nº 001/2026 na íntegra e seus anexos continuam disponíveis para consulta no portal da Prefeitura de Macaé .

articles.title: Banco Master: entenda como funcionavam as operações que levaram a uma fraude bilionária | G1
articles.standfirst: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.summary: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.body:
O Banco Master está no centro de uma investigação sobre operações bilionárias. O banco levantava dinheiro por meio da venda de CDBs com juros altos. Os investimentos também atraíam clientes por contarem com a proteção do Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC), respeitados os limites da garantia.

Segundo a Polícia Federal, o BRB, controlado pelo governo do Distrito Federal, pagou cerca de R$ 17 bilhões ao Master pela compra de carteiras de crédito. Desse total, R$ 12,2 bilhões estão sob investigação porque, segundo as apurações, os créditos não existiam. Regimes de previdência de servidores de estados e municípios também tinham cerca de R$ 1,8 bilhão aplicado no banco.

Em novembro de 2025, o Banco Central determinou a liquidação do Master, citando uma grave crise de liquidez, o comprometimento da situação financeira e violações às regras do sistema financeiro. O caso ainda pode ter novos desdobramentos na Justiça.

articles.title: Dólar abre em alta, de olho em preços do petróleo e pesquisas eleitorais | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana subiu 0,70%, cotada a R$ R$ 5,0105. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 0,74%, aos 204.309 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana subiu 0,70%, cotada a R$ R$ 5,0105. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 0,74%, aos 204.309 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar abriu a sessão desta quinta-feira (8) em alta, com um avanço de 0,15% perto das 9h, cotado R$ 5,0178 . Já as negociações do Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, começam às 10h.

Investidores acompanham a disparada nos preços do petróleo, após notícias de que o governo Trump pode fazer novos ataques ao Irã. Dados do mercado de trabalho americano e sinais sobre o futuro dos juros no país também ficam no radar. Por aqui, o cenário eleitoral segue em foco.

▶️Sinais de que o governo Trump planeja realizar novos ataques contra o Irã antes das eleições legislativas voltaram a pressionar os preços do petróleo nesta quinta-feira. Somado aos novos ataques a petroleiros no Estreito de Ormuz, investidores seguem preocupados com os efeitos da guerra nos preços globais de energia.

Com o noticiário, os preços do petróleo operavam em alta nesta quinta-feira. Perto das 9h, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, subia 4,37%, cotado a US$ 104,58 . Já o West Texas Intermediate ( WTI ), referência dos EUA, avançava 4,49% , a US$ 92,24 o barril.

▶️ Na agenda econômica, o destaque fica com os novos dados de emprego dos Estados Unidos . Os números devem trazer novos sinais sobre a força da economia americana e pode ajudar analistas a calibrarem suas apostas para os juros do país.

▶️ No Brasil, o foco fica com as novas pesquisas eleitorais do Datafolha , com os números da corrida presidencial e da disputa pelos governos do Rio de Janeiro e do Distrito Federal. Os levantamentos foram contratados pela Globo e pelo jornal Folha de S.Paulo.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Investidores aguardam os números das novas pesquisas eleitorais. Na véspera, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidato à Presidência no segundo turno, disse que pretende aproveitar a maioria de seu grupo político no Congresso para mudar a Constituição, caso seja eleito.

Durante evento em Goiânia, após receber o apoio de Ronaldo Caiado e Daniel Vilela, o candidato afirmou que quer eleger um aliado para a presidência da Câmara e usar essa composição para promover as mudanças, mas não especificou quais pontos da Constituição pretendia alterar.

Nesta quarta-feira (7), Flávio explicou que a declaração sobre “mudar a Constituição para redemocratizar o país” se referia a propostas que já defendeu, como a redução da maioridade penal, mudanças no Judiciário, alterações na reforma tributária e o fim da reeleição.

O candidato disse que essas mudanças teriam de ser feitas por meio de Propostas de Emenda à Constituição (PECs) e afirmou que pretende agir com “ponderação” e respeito à Constituição.

A reforma do Judiciário e a redução da maioridade penal já aparecem entre suas propostas.

🔍 Para aprovar uma mudança na Constituição, é preciso apresentar uma PEC, que passa por dois turnos de votação na Câmara e no Senado e precisa de pelo menos três quintos dos votos em cada Casa — 308 deputados e 49 senadores .

A Constituição também estabelece limites às mudanças, como a proteção às chamadas cláusulas pétreas, que incluem direitos e garantias individuais, voto direto e secreto e a separação dos Poderes.

Na segunda (5), o mercado reagiu com forte alta após Flávio terminar o primeiro turno à frente de Lula . Economistas, porém, alertam que o otimismo pode ser passageiro, diante da falta de propostas concretas para as contas públicas e dos desafios políticos para aprová-las.

Na Ásia , houve queda generalizada entre as bolsas da região, conforme investidores repercutiam novas tensões políticas, rendimentos globais mais elevados a temporada de balanços corporativos locais.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai, caiu 0,8%, enquanto o CSI300 , índice que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzen, perdeu 1,09%. Entre os demais índices da região, o Nikkei , do Japão, recuou 1,42%, o Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, teve queda de 2,62% e o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, desvalorizou 1,43%.

articles.title: US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary property
articles.summary: Your father has several properties in his and decides to sell one of them. Do you as a daughter have a claim on the property?
articles.body: Your father has several properties in his and decides to sell one of them. Do you as a daughter have a claim on the property? In one such case, a daughter who sought a share in properties held by her father has lost her legal battle after the Karnataka High Court held that she failed to prove that the properties were ancestral or coparcenary properties in which she had acquired a right by birth.The case involved a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman’s father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property, giving her a right to seek partition under the Hindu Succession Act.What the case is aboutThe woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them after her father sold one property. The daughter sued her parents and sister for partition of four family properties. Her case was that the properties formed part of the Hindu joint family estate and that she was entitled to a share as a coparcener.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claimsShe also sought rights in movable and immovable assets, including family jewellery, bank deposits, share investments and debentures, which she alleged were joint family properties.The suit covered four schedule properties.The woman claimed that Schedule A was ancestral property which had fallen to her father's share. She further claimed that income generated through quarrying on that property had been used to acquire Schedule B. She also claimed that her father had inherited Schedules C and D and that the income from the family properties had contributed to the family's other assets.Her legal argument relied significantly on Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act as amended with effect from September 9, 2005. The amended provision recognises a daughter as a coparcener by birth in a Mitakshara joint Hindu family, with the same rights as a son in coparcenary property.The trial court rejected the daughter’s claim and dismissed the suit. She then approached the High Court where she lost again.Why did the High Court rule against the daughter?The Karnataka High Court considered whether Schedules A, C and D were the self-acquired properties of the woman’s father or whether he had inherited them from his ancestors in a manner that made them joint Hindu family properties.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleThe evidence of the daughter’s own witness became important.Her paternal uncle said Schedule A had been purchased by his father. He also admitted that the portion forming Schedule A had come to the woman’s father's share and that it was absolute property.His evidence regarding Schedule C was similar. He stated that it had also been purchased by his father and that, in the partition, Schedule C came to the woman’s father's share. He agreed that Schedule C was the father's absolute property.The High Court also found that Schedule D was the self-acquired property of the woman’s grandfather and that it came to her father's share as a result of partition.“The said witness clearly admits that the property fell to the share of defendant No.1 under the said partition/ family arrangement is his self-acquired property,” the court said.“The admissions given by PW.2 clearly indicate that the properties partitioned were the self-acquired properties of the grandfather. In such an eventuality, there cannot be any adverse opinion against the defendants for their failure to lead evidence, when the plaintiff, herself, has failed to discharge the initial burden casted upon her,” the court said.The court therefore concluded that Schedules A, C and D were not ancestral or coparcenary properties. They had become the individual and separate properties of the woman's father."These properties are neither the joint Hindu family properties nor coparcenery properties. These properties became individual/separate properties of defendant No.1,” the court said.The High Court then examined the significance of Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act.It noted that the 2005 amendment made a daughter a coparcener by birth in a Mitakshara joint Hindu family and gave her the same rights as a son in coparcenary property. But the court stressed that the right arises in coparcenary property, not in every property owned by a parent."Thus if a property is joint Hindu family property, then only a coparcener shall acquire the right by birth and not otherwise,” it said.The High Court specifically said that if the properties in Schedules A, C and D were the grandfather's self-acquired properties, he had the right to dispose of them. Once they came to his children through the partition, they became the separate properties of those children rather than retaining a coparcenary character.The court also considered Schedule B. The Karnataka High Court's analysis stated that, even according to the woman’s case, Schedule B had been purchased from income generated from Schedule A and treated it as the father's self-acquired property. The High Court ultimately found that the woman had failed to establish that the properties claimed by her were coparcenary properties.The court said, “There was no unity of ownership and possession between all members of the family. The plaintiff was never in possession of the property, which became the self-acquired properties of her father. In the absence of unity of possession of the plaintiff along with other family members i.e. parents and defendant No.3/sister. The plaintiff did not acquire an interest by birth in the properties, which are the individual/separate properties of her father.”“It is well settled that Mitakshara father has absolute right of disposition over his self-acquired property, to which no exception can be taken by male/female descendants,” it added.Explaining the judgement, Gaurav Dasgupta, Partner, Khaitan & Co said, “The Court drew the line clearly. What the grandfather bought with his own money was his self-acquired property, and he was free to deal with it as he wished. When he handed it to his children through a family partition, it became each child's separate property. It did not become joint family property in which grandchildren acquire rights at birth.”“The Court added that the result is the same whether the children received it through a partition or by ordinary inheritance. A daughter's right as a coparcener applies only where the property actually has a coparcenary character, and she must prove that character first,” he tells TOI.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claimSignificance of rulingGaurav Dasgupta says daughter's right by birth covers ancestral property, not her father's own property or even a property which has been gifted to her father or her father had acquired by way of a partition/settlement from his own father.“Only when a person inherits a property from any one of his three immediate paternal ancestors, his sons, grandsons and great grandsons, acquire an interest in it by birth or under Section 6 of the Hindus Succession act, after amendment w.e.f. 09.09.2005,” he tells TOI.According to Dasgupta, this judgment is a timely reminder that the landmark 2005 reform giving daughters equal coparcenary rights is powerful, but it is not a blank cheque.“Many people now assume that a daughter can claim a share in anything her father owns. That is not the law, and this ruling explains why. However, post the death of the father, in case of intestate succession, she will be treated equally like her siblings at the time of determination of succession,” he adds.According to Dasgupta, what this settles is the distinction families most often get wrong: 'property from my grandfather' is not automatically 'ancestral property'. What it leaves open is what happens after the father dies. His separate property then passes under the ordinary succession rules, unless he has made a will or a gift. That is a separate claim, and this partition suit did not decide it, he says.He advises that before suing for partition, it’s important to trace how each property was first acquired and collect the documents, such as old partition deeds and purchase records.You use AI every day. articles.title: Survey: 12% in India report being scammed in last 1 year
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A survey conducted by GSMA, a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, has found 12% of respondents in India reported being scammed
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A survey conducted by GSMA, a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, has found 12% of respondents in India reported being scammed in the last 12 months as opposed to 8% in Asean-6 - Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam and Philippines."Indian consumers also extend institutions an unusual level of permission to use their data," said the India Consumer Scam Report 2026."Online shopping scams, at 33%, are the most common type in India compared with 32% across Asean-6, followed by prize, lottery and inheritance scams at 31%, compared with 25% (Asean-6), and job or income scams at 30%, compared with 32%. Scams using a QR code or payment link stand at 27% in India, compared to 18% across Asean-6 and 23% in Thailand. Messaging apps are the most common route, involved in 42% of Indian victims' scams against 41% across Asean-6," said the report.GSMA chief regulatory officer John Giusti told TOI that the challenge of digital economy frauds is growing globally and telecom operators in India, along with authorities here, are at the "forefront" of tackling the menace. "One trillion dollars were lost to scams worldwide in 2024 and 50% of consumers (globally) have said they're being exposed to scams."India led the way in 5G rollout globally and has a significant headstart in 6G too. Telecom operators here are leading the way in tackling the menace. Your phone just flashed a likely spam and that shows the attempt being made to safeguard consumers," said Giusti."Whether it be scam calls, scam advertisements on digital platforms, scammers are trying to find ways to infiltrate financial services. Globally everyone needs to come together and solve this problem," he said.GSMA has used these findings on a cross-sectional online survey of adults in India and the six Asean markets through self-administered online interviews between July 29, 2026 and Aug 3 with about 500 respondents in India.You use AI every day. articles.title: Premium spirits sales soar past cheaper liquor: Report
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Premium spirits are growing several times faster than cheaper liquor in India, with higher-priced products gaining a larger share of sales,
articles.body: BENGALURU: Premium spirits are growing several times faster than cheaper liquor in India, with higher-priced products gaining a larger share of sales, according to a report by industry body International Spirits and Wines Association of India (ISWAI).Sales volumes in the premium segment grew at a compound annual rate of 10.2% between 2022 and 2025. That compares with 1.1% for the report's lowest-priced category and 1.4% for regular spirits. Overall spirits volumes grew 3.7% annually over the same period. Super-premium Indian-made spirits grew even faster, at about 34% annually. However, this segment remains small, accounting for less than 1% of total spirits volumes in the report's 2025 estimates.Cheaper products continue to account for a substantial part of the market. The lowest-priced and regular categories together made up nearly half of spirits sales volumes in 2025. Their slower growth nevertheless points to a change in the mix of products being sold."Rising incomes, evolving consumer aspirations, and greater availability of premium products are reshaping the market mix," the report said.It also linked the shift to changes in liquor retailing. Stores offering wider selections, better product displays and space for customers to browse are encouraging shoppers to explore brands and spend more, according to the report.Indian malt whiskies were among the faster-growing categories. Their volumes expanded at about 39% annually between 2022 and 2025, compared with about 5% for Scotch malts, the report estimated. It said Indian malts overtook Scotch malts in sales volumes in 2024.Imported spirits also grew faster than the broader spirits market, although their share remained modest. Their volumes rose about 8% annually over the three years, taking their market share from 2.4% to 2.7%. ISWAI estimated India's alcoholic beverages market at about Rs 6.2 lakh crore ($71 billion).You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: At 107, National Company Law Tribunal OKs record insolvency cases
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved a record 107 corporate insolvency cases during the last quarter, but stares at the prospect
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved a record 107 corporate insolvency cases during the last quarter, but stares at the prospect of a moderation in the pace due to a large number of vacancies.Data released by NCLT estimated the value of cases approved at Rs 11,000 crore during the Sept quarter, as against Rs 5,500 crore involved in the June quarter when 78 cases were approved. During Oct-Dec 2025, the tribunal had approved 90 cases, the previous high. Since April 2017, it has cleared 1,735 cases with 185 approved so far this fiscal, as against 257 during 2025-26.During the last quarter, the Mumbai bench approved 35 resolution plans, followed by 29 by the principal bench and the New Delhi bench.At the end of Sept, there were 335 pending cases across its 12 benches, as against 363 in April-end. Of the pending cases, orders have been reserved in 41 cases, with the Supreme Court, high courts and NCLAT ordering a stay in 24.With no member appointed since the start of 2025, barring the president Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, NCLT is 14 members short of the sanctioned strength of 62, with four more retiring by Dec."As a result, 13 courts are functioning on a full-day basis and 18 on a half-day basis," said NCLT.It is also facing another challenge -- the ratio between judicial and administrative strength. Judicial members currently outnumber technical members 26 to 22, making it difficult to constitute benches as each bench requires representation from both categories. While govt has initiated the process of selecting new members, the exercise is time-consuming and members also have to undergo training after they join.The tribunal is urging members to clear cases at a faster pace with the president also monitoring the performance of the benches across the country.You use AI every day. articles.title: Consolidated account statements to reflect deposits in banks
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Individuals may soon find it easier to see their financial assets in one place.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Individuals may soon find it easier to see their financial assets in one place. RBI on Wednesday announced two measures: making account aggregators interoperable and allowing bank-deposit information to be added to the monthly consolidated account statement (CAS), which currently captures holdings such as shares, mutual funds and pensions. The move will make it easier for survivors of deceased account holders to discover their financial assets and reduce the number of unclaimed deposits.Interoperability will allow customers to use any account aggregator to access and share financial information held across different banks and other financial-information providers. With about 15 account aggregators, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said information was fragmented; linking them would make it easier for individuals, insurers, asset managers and investment advisers to use it, with the customer's consent.Account aggregators let customers securely consolidate and share financial data from multiple banks and financial institutions with their consent. For lenders, this provides a faster view of income, cash flows and liabilities for credit assessment; for personal-finance apps, it brings fragmented financial information into one dashboard.RBI is also facilitating the inclusion of bank deposits in CAS through account aggregators. Demat holders will thus be able to see securities and bank deposits together, while those without demat accounts will continue to obtain and share a consolidated view of their financial information through account aggregators.You use AI every day. articles.title: Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist
articles.summary: Oil prices inched higher on Thursday as concerns over supply from the Middle East intensified amid a rise in attacks on vessels in the Gulf and the Strait
articles.body: Oil prices inched higher on Thursday as concerns over supply from the Middle East intensified amid a rise in attacks on vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude was trading at $101.50 a barrel, up $1.32 or 1.32%, while WTI crude stood at $89.28, gaining $1 or 1.13%.The latest gains come despite a fall in prices in the previous session, when the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up the release of oil stocks and give priority to diesel supplies. The plan, launched in March, is aimed at dealing with record fuel prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has become a growing concern as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month. Before the war, the route handled shipments equivalent to about 20% of global oil and fuel supplies.The pressure on shipping has increased even as Gulf producers raise exports. Tanker attacks through the Strait reached their highest level last week for any week since the Iran war began, leaving crude shipments facing higher costs and greater risks for cargoes and crew.A tanker north of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles in the latest attack, causing casualties, the United Kingdom maritime trade operations agency said on Wednesday.Supply concerns were accompanied by signs of tighter US inventories. According to Reuters, American crude stocks fell by 3.2 million barrels in the week ended October 2 to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration. The decline was larger than the 1.7 million-barrel fall analysts had expected in a Reuters poll.Diesel and jet fuel inventories also declined, with distillate fuel stocks falling by 42,000 barrels to 105.14 million barrels. Those inventories remained below their levels for this period of the year over the past five years.Oil markets have remained unsettled for more than seven months since the Middle East conflict began. articles.title: Stocks fall further as oil spike fans fresh inflation worries
articles.summary: Equities extended losses Thursday as inflation fears were stoked by a fresh jump in oil prices following a report that said Donald Trump was considering more...
articles.body:
Equities extended losses Thursday as inflation fears were stoked by a fresh jump in oil prices following a report that said Donald Trump was considering more Iran strikes ahead of next month's US midterm elections.

The selling tracked a retreat on Wall Street, where tech firms pulled back from recent gains, having weathered concerns over spiking borrowing costs and geopolitical uncertainty.

Crude had started the week on the back foot thanks to signs that exports from the Middle East were heading back towards pre-war levels and that G7 nations had agreed to tap their stockpiles.

But anxiety returned as figures showed Tehran had increased strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthis rebutted claims they had lost key territory and top oil officials warned that global reserves were running worryingly low.

And on Wednesday, The Atlantic reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon to draw up options to hit sites in Iran ahead of the midterms, with Trump's Republicans in danger of losing both houses of Congress.

The article said the size and targets were still being discussed, but added that a wider operation could be in the works after the polls on November 3.

It added that even its proponents did not think the attacks would bring Tehran to talks or see Hormuz reopened, but hoped they would show strength leading into the vote.

Both main crude contracts rose more than one percent Thursday, with supplies also hit by the loss of more than 500,000 barrels of Gulf of Mexico output owing to producers shutting up shop as Tropical Storm Isaias approaches.

News that International Energy Agency members were ready to tap more oil from reserves did little to assuage worried traders.

The spike in oil prices fanned inflation fears again and put fresh upward pressure on government bond yields to multi-year highs.

After all three main indexes on Wall Street dropped -- with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq off records -- Asia followed suit.

Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei and Manila were all well down, though Shanghai edged up as investors returned from a week-long break.

US Federal Reserve officials expect to hike interest rates again before the end of the year, according to minutes of their September meeting, where everyone agreed to the first increase since July 2023.

"With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end," the minutes said.

articles.title: US mortgage rates jump to 7.49%, hit highest level in nearly 3 years
articles.summary: US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years, with the sharp rise in borrowing costs adding to pressure on the housing
articles.body: US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years, with the sharp rise in borrowing costs adding to pressure on the housing market as Americans head towards November 3 elections.The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) said, as cited by Reuters. This spike pushed rates to the highest level since November 2023, hitting demand for home loans.Mortgage applications dropped 4.2% last week from the previous week, while refinancing applications fell sharply. Overall application volumes are now at their lowest since February 2025 and have declined nearly 50% since January."Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist told Reuters.Mortgage rates have closely followed movements in the yield on 10-year US treasury notes. Earlier this week, the yield topped 5.3%, reaching a 24-year high, with concerns over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth driving the rise.Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar increase in the 10-year treasury yield.The increase comes at a politically sensitive time, with the US mid-term elections just four weeks away. The cost of living was the top issue among Americans in deciding how they would vote, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday. At the same time, US President Donald Trump's approval rating stood at a record low of 32%.Inflation has also risen, reaching 3.4% in August on a measure targeted by the Federal Reserve at 2%.Fed policymakers have signalled that they expect another interest-rate increase by the end of the year following the rate hike in September. Markets are currently betting that policymakers will not raise rates at the next meeting at the end of October.The latest increase in mortgage rates comes as affordability remains under pressure for buyers, while the decline in loan applications points to weaker activity in the mortgage market.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'India's regulatory framework non-discriminatory,' govt responds to Musk
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has rejected Elon Musk’s allegation that Starlink is being “being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has rejected Elon Musk’s allegation that Starlink is being “being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people.” Govt said in a statement Thursday that “India's regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory” and that “the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived.”Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Starlink are the three entities plan to start satellite communication services in India. “Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage,” govt statement added.Musk had on Wednesday said on X: “We are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are… This is a crime against the people of India!”The statement came on a day when Lauren Dreyer, VP of Starlink Business Operations, said at the India Mobile Congress that “We stand ready to serve India, as soon as India is ready.” “For years we have been setting the foundation for the same type of relationship (that Starlink has in countries were it operates) here in India, establishing MoUs with Jio, Airtel and more; working closely with state Govts to listen and learn how Starlink might be able to best serve once it is authorised,” she said at IMC.“Starlink can help reach places where the last mile is still the hardest mile, working alongside India’s operators, govt and industry. As India works through the final approvals, our message is simple: We stand ready to serve India, as soon as India is ready,” Dreyer added.Starlink has tried to allay India’s security fears by claiming that Indian user data will be kept in the country and having security controls as per the country’s requirement.Given strained India-US ties over multiple issues like the stuck trade deal, threat of tariffs over buying Russian oil and most importantly security concerns over Starlink, people in the know say Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio are likely to get the nod before Musk, whose wait could be much longer.You use AI every day. articles.title: A hurricane could cripple US refining when the world can least afford it
articles.summary: The global energy system is already being pushed to the brink. A hurricane barreling down on America’s refining nerve center is the last thing that’s needed.
articles.body: The global energy system is already being pushed to the brink. A hurricane barreling down on America’s refining nerve center is the last thing that’s needed. Isaias, the Atlantic season’s first hurricane, is arriving at a time when there is almost no margin for error. US refineries, mostly located along the Gulf Coast, are running as hard as they can to offset war-driven outages overseas. Fuel inventories that act as shock absorbers have already been tapped. And America’s emergency oil stockpile is at the lowest level since 1982. Hurricane Isaias “could be a gigantic event. It’s the worst time something like this could happen in 25 years,” said Robert Yawger, director of energy futures at Mizuho Securities. The actual impact of Isaias will depend on the storm’s path and intensity. Current forecasts call for the storm to hit east of New Orleans, a major refining hub, which should spare vital energy infrastructure from the storm’s worst. Still, major oil producers including Shell, Chevron and BP have evacuated non-essential personnel from oil platforms in the Gulf and curtailed production. As of midday Wednesday, about 512,000 barrels per day of Gulf of Mexico oil production had been shut in, according to the federal agency Marine Minerals Administration. That amounts to about 25% of the region’s production. And about 16% of current natural gas production in the Gulf of Mexico has been sidelined. The risk is that the storm’s damage could squeeze supply chains even more, further raising historically high prices. The Iran war, combined with Ukrainian drone attacks in Russia and export restrictions in China, have catapulted diesel prices to all-time highs. Gasoline was more than $4.40 per gallon last week and has never been this expensive at this time of year. Shock absorbers have shrunk About 2.7 million barrels per day, or 14%, of America’s refining capacity, lie within or near the projected of the path of the storm, according to Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates. Lipow said he expects at least some refineries in the New Orleans/Baton Rouge and Mississippi/Alabama regions will have to slow down how much oil they turn into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. Tankers delivering oil to refineries and loading fuel out of refineries could get delayed as well. This would particularly impact Florida because the state relies on shipments of fuel from the Gulf Coast. “There is no slack in the system to make up for lost refinery capacity. Lost production will have to come out of already low commercial inventories,” Lipow wrote in an email. Those commercial inventories have been whittled away. Gasoline stockpiles recently fell to their lowest seasonal record since 2012, according to federal data. Distillate inventories, which include mostly diesel, are at their lowest level for early October since tracking started in the early 1980s. Not only that, but the Strategic Petroleum Reserve has been aggressively drained to ease the energy shock. The SPR now holds about 283 million barrels of crude, the least since 1982 when the emergency reserve was being filled during the Reagan administration. ‘It would be a disaster’ Refineries in the Middle East have been damaged by the Iran war, or have struggled to get shipments out to the rest of the world. Refineries in Russia have been destroyed or damaged by drone attacks. And China, seeking to avoid fuel shortages, has restricted its exports. US refineries, operating at about 95% of their capacity, are one of the remaining key sources for the global fuel supply. “It would be a disaster if US refining capacity has to come off the market. It would basically force a diesel export ban,” said Yawger, the Mizuho executive, who added that he is not in favor of restricting US diesel exports. Much depends on the intensity of the storm, including the severity of flooding and wind damage. Isaias could peak as a Category 2 storm with 110 mph winds by early Friday, but is expected to weaken somewhat before landfall. Even with a Category 1 hurricane, it can take a week to return refining operations to normal.

articles.title: Majority of states urge Supreme Court to consider prediction market regulation
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of states are backing New Jersey’s request for the Supreme Court to declare that states can regulate prediction markets, warning that lower judges are “hopelessly confused and divided.” Last month, New Jersey petitioned the justices to decide the issue that has been bubbling up in the lower courts. The justices turn away…
articles.body:
A bipartisan group of states are backing New Jersey’s request for the Supreme Court to declare that states can regulate prediction markets , warning that lower judges are “hopelessly confused and divided.”

Last month, New Jersey petitioned the justices to decide the issue that has been bubbling up in the lower courts. The justices turn away the vast majority of cases but are set to consider hearing it at a closed-door meeting later this term.

Major platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket — supported by the Trump administration — say the federal government should be in control, not states.

“The prediction markets are wrong,” the group of states wrote in their amicus brief supporting New Jersey, docketed on Wednesday.

“They cannot strip the States of their core sovereign power through relabeling and window-dressing,” the brief continued. “Our constitutional structure is much more durable than that. And the promise of federalism ensures that States do not lose their ability to protect their citizens so easily.”

The bipartisan coalition was led by Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson (R) and joined by the District of Columbia and 38 other states

States retain broad authority to regulate and tax gambling in their borders, but prediction markets argue their products are distinct from those traditional offerings.

Platforms like Kalshi say their products should be deemed “swaps” under federal law, which would place it under the authority of the federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). The states, however, said that theory would undermine their gambling regulations , arguing it eliminates “guardrails” and threatens their citizens’ safety.

“That almost all the nation’s States have spoken with one voice on the matter should be enough,” they wrote.

The case arrived at the Supreme Court after Kalshi sued New Jersey last year to block the state from enforcing its gambling laws against the company. The company won before the 3 rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, part of an emerging split among the appeals courts around the country.

As the Garden State now brings the issue to the justices for the first time, it has also garnered support from the National Football League (NFL).

The NFL raised concerns about whether the CFTC has sufficient resources to ensure prediction markets “do not jeopardize game integrity.”

“All this stands in stark contrast to state gaming authorities, which have engaged with the NFL for years to establish structural safeguards that provide core integrity protections,” the NFL wrote in its brief , filed on Thursday.

articles.title: Payments could come soon in $177M AT&T settlement: How much will you receive?
articles.summary: Millions of AT&T customers who had their personal data leaked in a data breach (or two) may soon be receiving their portions of a $177 million settlement.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Millions of AT&T customers who had their personal data leaked in a data breach (or two) may soon be receiving their portions of a $177 million settlement .

A pair of lawsuits were previously brought against AT&T following breaches that the company confirmed happened in 2019 and 2022.

In the first breach, the personal information of about 7.6 million then-current account holders and 65.4 million former account holders was found in a dataset on the “dark web.” In the second, the data of nearly all of its customers was found to have been downloaded to a third-party platform.

Two funds — one for $149 million, the other for $28 million — were established as part of the settlement. AT&T previously denied the allegations in a statement to Nexstar but said it had “agreed to this settlement to avoid the expense and uncertainty of protracted litigation.”

The settlement received final approval from the court last week, administrators said in an update to the settlement website, which means approved class members could soon see payments of up to $7,500 hit their accounts.

That will vary based on which breach impacted you, but regardless, you had to have filed a claim before the Dec. 18, 2025, deadline. More than 4.9 million claims were submitted, according to court documents. Nearly 1.1 million were “rejected as late, duplicate, fraudulent, released, withdrawn, or ineligible business.”

If you were among the more than 3 million claims approved, you could receive up to $7,500, according to court documents. To qualify here, you needed to have “proper proof” of documented losses that were “fairly traceable.”

For all others, there were tiered payout options. If your Social Security number was included in the breach, you could have made a claim for a Tier 1 payment. If any other data was included, but not your Social Security number, you could have filed a claim for a Tier 2 payment. A third tier was available to those also impacted by the second data breach, with payments sent to be disbursed as a pro rata share, or an equal share of whatever remained in the settlement fund after other payments were sent out.

A claimant could file for a Tier 1 or Tier 2 payment, and a Tier 3, if they were impacted by both under the settlement proposal.

Court documents show roughly how much class members in each tier can receive.

For those whose Social Security numbers were impacted by the 2019 breach, and thereby eligible for Tier 1 funds, the payments will range between $39 and $40, according to court documents on the approved settlement. More than 1.6 million Tier 1 claims were approved.

Tier 2 payments will range between $7.50 and $8.10, while payments for those who qualified for Tier 3 will range between $6.50 and $7.10. There were more than 680,000 Tier 2 claims approved and more than 1.5 million in Tier 3.

That depends on whether there are any objections to the court order. The order, filed on Oct. 2, did address several objections already, however.

It also calls for payments to be distributed within 60 days after the effective date.
